newsitem.title: UK: UK health reform care investment trust launched.
newsitem.headline: UK health reform care investment trust launched.

text.p: HealthReform Partners (HRP), a subsidiary of a U.S. asset management firm, will launch the U.K.'s first healthcare investment trust to capitalise on the $2.5 trillion market worldwide.
The Healthcare Reform Investment Trust will focus on companies benefiting from global healthcare reform, cost containment and industry consolidation, an HRP statement said.
David Talbot, president of HRP, said the fund would concentrate on medical devices and services, which in aggregate account for 90 percent of healthcare industry spending.
"Investment trusts that specialise in pharmeceuticals and biotechnology are accessing only 10 percent of the industry spending," he said.

The fund's launch target is 20 million stg. Initially, about 85 percent of the assets will be invested in the U.S. and 15 percent in Europe. Over the medium term, 80 percent will be in the U.S., 10 percent in Europe and 10 percent in the Far East.
Returns for the 10-year fund may be enhanced by borrowing up to 25 percent of the investment trust's net assets.
Launch costs are about three percent of funds raised, and the placing, expected to close in mid-October, will be sponsored by HSBC James Capel and Rauscher Pierce & Clark.
There is an annual management fee of one percent plus a 20-percent performance fee payable on outperformance of the S&P Healthcare Composite Index, subject to positive net asset value returns.

HRP is a wholly owned subsidiary of Melhado Flynn & Associates Inc, a specialist New York-based asset management firm regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission, with around $1.0 billion of funds under management.
